name: Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys

reason: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent.
research: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.

name: Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys

reason: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real.
research: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
